_about: Optional written view per upcoming game, keyed by ESPN game id: {"text": "...", "sources": [urls], "written_at": ISO}. Shown on the game page as 'Analyst view' (locker-room news, trade rumours, a player facing his former team...). Never mixed into the numbers.

401910036.text: Memphis had their franchise-record eight-game road winning streak snapped 104-95 in Minnesota on Saturday and are still without rookie Cameron Boozer (ankle), though Ty Jerome is back and scored 18. Charlotte have lost 10 of 11 and come home from an 0-4 road trip; Moussa Diabate, in a contract year, is rebounding well and says the team needs urgency. Memphis come in rested and stung by the loss, so the angle leans Memphis.

401910037.text: Philadelphia go for a sixth straight win; Jaylen Brown (hamstring), Dean Wade and Adem Bona are all listed probable. Portland have lost three of four, blew a late lead on a Mikal Bridges buzzer-beater in New York, and Damian Lillard said 'we can't let this trend continue'; Ja Morant remains out. Portland are mid six-game road trip and frustrated, so the angle leans Philadelphia.

401910038.text: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is out with a back injury, and OKC played Sunday in Miami with only nine available players, three of them on two-way deals. Indiana have lost four straight, are 3-10 without Tyrese Haliburton, and Yahoo reports a souring mood and trade chatter. Both sides are on a back-to-back, but OKC's depleted rotation makes this the softest spot they have had; the angle leans Indiana.

401910039.text: Milwaukee have lost 13 straight, two shy of the franchise-record skid, but their last five losses were all by 10 points or fewer and Tyler Herro just scored a career-high 50. Toronto snapped a six-game slide on a Scottie Barnes game-winner, but are without Kawhi Leonard and RJ Barrett (out at least two weeks). The Bucks are competing hard despite the record, so the angle leans slightly towards Milwaukee keeping it close.

401910040.text: Julius Randle returns to Minnesota for the first time since the Wolves traded him to Brooklyn over the summer, and he leads the Nets at 21.1 points a game. Brooklyn are 3-12, without Nolan Traore, and front-office talk is about shopping Michael Porter Jr. and other veterans. Minnesota have thrived without Anthony Edwards; Randle's motivation is real, but the angle still leans Minnesota.

401910041.text: Chicago are without their top two scorers, Norman Powell (hamstring) and rookie Caleb Wilson (broken hand), and coach Tiago Splitter is leaning on 'next guy up'. Cleveland have won three of four since early-season pressure on Kenny Atkinson, with 37-year-old James Harden coming off a 51-point night. The angle leans Cleveland.

401910042.text: New Orleans are a trade-market story: Dejounte Murray requested a trade on Nov 13 (and is out injured), and teams are asking about Zion Williamson, Trey Murphy III and Herb Jones. Zion (thigh) and Murphy are listed probable after leaving the San Antonio loss early. Phoenix have won three straight; the unsettled Pelicans locker room leans this towards Phoenix.

401910043.text: Brandon Ingram makes his Clippers debut after Achilles surgery, which brings energy but also minutes limits and rust; the Clippers have lost three straight and may sell veterans after losing draft picks. Houston open a five-game homestand at full strength, with Alperen Sengun available and Clint Capela back from a 10-game absence. The angle leans Houston.

401910044.text: This is a revenge spot: Utah beat the Lakers 109-97 in Los Angeles last Wednesday. The Jazz are on a back-to-back after a 116-114 loss in Dallas and are without Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic. Austin Reaves is out again, but Quentin Grimes has thrived in his place. The angle leans the Lakers.

401910045.text: De'Aaron Fox (shin) is questionable for a return to Sacramento, Victor Wembanyama is questionable with back tightness, and Dylan Harper is out. The Kings just ended an eight-game skid by beating Boston, but coach Doug Christie is in a lame-duck year and Domantas Sabonis was reported earlier this month to want out. Spurs absences could tighten it, but the angle still leans San Antonio.

401909314.text: Both teams lost on Sunday: Detroit at Atlanta, with Cade Cunningham held to 5 points and the frontcourt missing Jalen Duren; Orlando by 20 in Washington without Paolo Banchero (high ankle sprain). Duncan Robinson is due for re-evaluation around now. Orlando had been on a 5-1 run sparked by coach Sean Sweeney's viral huddle, but without Banchero the angle leans slightly Detroit.

401909315.text: Boston have lost four straight, the first such streak under Joe Mazzulla, all in clutch games, and Derrick White is 3-of-25 from three over his last three. Paul George sat Sunday for rest and is expected back. Washington have won three straight after an 0-8 start, while Anthony Davis plays amid trade interest and no extension. The angle leans Boston bouncing back, but the Wizards' form makes it closer than the records.

401909316.text: Dallas are on a back-to-back after nearly blowing a 16-point lead to Utah, with Cooper Flagg admitting the team 'got complacent'; P.J. Washington (illness) has missed two games. Denver have won five of six after Jamal Murray's 45 and a Nikola Jokic triple-double in an overtime win in Chicago. The angle leans Denver.
